comments.body:
**Correctness: a later `COMMENTED` review silently erases an earlier `APPROVED` from the same reviewer.**

Line 56 keeps only the last non-`PENDING` review per login. GitHub does not treat a `COMMENTED` review as withdrawing an approval, but this does.

Failure scenario: `coderabbitai[bot]` posts `APPROVED` (id 5) on head `H`; CodeRabbit's incremental pass then posts a `COMMENTED` review with inline notes (id 6) on the same head `H`. `latest['coderabbitai[bot]']` becomes the `COMMENTED` review, the `state=='APPROVED'` test at line 59 fails, line 79 appends `'independent current-head approval missing'`, and the PR never merges even though its approval stands on GitHub.

This is fail-closed, so it is a liveness rather than a safety defect — but `.coderabbit.yaml` sets `auto_incremental_review: true` and `auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits: 0`, so extra `COMMENTED` reviews on an already-approved head are the expected steady state, not an edge case. The delivery path will likely never fire in practice.

`tests/test_delivery_controller.py:51` (`test_comment_is_not_approval`) mutates the single approval into a comment, and `:59` (`test_latest_changes_requested_blocks`) appends a `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Neither covers APPROVED-then-COMMENTED. Suggest tracking the latest `APPROVED`/`CHANGES_REQUESTED`/`DISMISSED` review per login and ignoring `COMMENTED` for approval state, with a test for that ordering.

Either drop the parameter and rely on `protection_ready()`, or pass the actual result of the CodeQL rule check through to `evaluate()` so the reason string corresponds to a real observation.

**The controller's sensitive-change consent gate is bypassable, because native auto-merge remains enabled alongside it.**

`docs/operations/github-automation-2026-09-23/repository-before.json` records `"allow_auto_merge": true`, and this PR does not change it. `ruleset-after.json:58` sets `required_approving_review_count: 1` with `required_reviewers: []`.

So the path that GitHub itself offers — enable auto-merge on a PR, let one approving review plus the required checks land it — is still open, and it applies none of the controls this PR builds: no `heleos-delivery` enrollment, no `automation-hold`, no activation-time floor, no commit attribution check, no exact-head `Heleos owner consent <sha>` comment for sensitive paths, no main-CI-before-next-delivery stop rule.

That matters most for the one control that is meant to be the backstop. A PR editing `.github/workflows/` or `CLAUDE.md` needs owner consent only if it goes through `delivery_controller.py`; routed through native auto-merge it needs a single approval.

Line 48's claim is narrower than it reads: the controller does not *itself* queue a native auto-merge that could outlive consent. True, and the merge-by-explicit-SHA design is the right call. But the section as a whole presents consent-for-sensitive-heads as the protection for sensitive changes, and at the repository level it is not enforced. Either disable `allow_auto_merge`, or state plainly that the consent gate binds only the controller path.

**Policy: CodeRabbit is not an admitted provider, and this file admits it.**

`docs/policies/egress.md` § 4 ends with: *"No other provider is admitted for repository content. Multi-provider or council-style routing of prompts is off."* Its only row is Anthropic. § 3 names exactly two permitted automated callers, `.github/workflows/claude-review.yml` and `.github/workflows/claude.yml`.

`.coderabbit.yaml` turns on automatic review of every PR (`base_branches: ['.*']`), which sends the PR diff and the repository content CodeRabbit reads to a second provider. `docs/policies/egress.md` § 2 classifies *"this repository's own design documents, roadmap, policies, workflow scripts, CI configuration, run records ... and the pull request diffs that carry them"* as `INTERNAL`, not `PUBLIC` — a public GitHub repository is not the `PUBLIC` data class, which the same table reserves for third-party published material with a logged license and origin.

`CLAUDE.md` § "Do not": *"Send `INTERNAL` or `PROJECT_CONFIDENTIAL` material to any external service, except where `docs/policies/egress.md` permits it for a named caller and provider once the owner has recorded the decision..."*

Spec § 11 additionally requires, for any third-party integration: *"source review, version pinning, minimum permissions, a named owner, and a concrete task"* and *"provenance, pinned version or digest, license, permissions and egress review, evaluation evidence, and a rollback target."* A hosted SaaS reviewer has no pinnable digest and is exactly the "may not drift at runtime" case that clause is about. No admission register entry, license record, or rollback target is added anywhere in this PR.

This needs an owner-signed amendment to the egress decision naming CodeRabbit as a provider and `delivery_controller.py` as a caller, before the config lands — not after.

**Policy: this is not a submission record, and its data class is wrong.**

Three separate problems with this line:

1. **`'classification':'PUBLIC'` is a misclassification.** `docs/policies/egress.md` § 2 puts *"this repository's own ... workflow scripts, CI configuration, run records, ... and the pull request diffs that carry them"* in `INTERNAL`. The source being a public repo does not move it into the `PUBLIC` class, which that table defines as published standards text, public manufacturer literature, public datasets/model cards and open-source code *with source and license logged in the admission register*. Declaring `PUBLIC` here is what lets the rest of the flow skip the `INTERNAL` controls.

2. **The field names are not the seven the spec requires.** `docs/policies/egress.md` § 5: *"Every external submission records the seven fields spec section 5 names, and only those"* — `provider, purpose, data_class, source_hashes, policy_decision, time, result_ref`. This record emits `provider, purpose, classification, source, authorization, time, state`: `data_class`, `source_hashes`, `policy_decision` and `result_ref` are all absent under those names. `tools/ci/checks.py:27` enforces exactly that tuple on `docs/runs/egress/index.jsonl`, so this record could not be rolled up into the ledger without failing `checks`.

3. **A `print()` to the Actions log is not where records live.** § 5 names the job summary, a workflow artifact, and after roll-up `docs/runs/egress/index.jsonl`. § 3 also says the record *"is a gate, not a log"*: both admitted callers run `tools/egress/record.py check` **before** the provider step, and the job fails if the policy or decision record is missing. `.github/workflows/delivery.yml` runs no such gate before this submission.

Spec § 13 likewise requires every production-changing decision to record *"actor, inputs, prior state, new state, reason, and time"*; the merge decision at line 184 is reported only by the `print(json.dumps(reports))` on line 189, which is discarded with the runner.

**Two defects on these two lines.**

**1. `'draft':False` contradicts the repository convention.** `CLAUDE.md` § "Conventions": *"Pull requests: opened as drafts into `main`; describe the problem, the change, how it was verified, and the run records it cites."* `CLAUDE.md` § "Branches" repeats it: *"open or update a **draft** pull request into `main`."* This publisher opens ready-for-review PRs, which is also what makes them immediately visible to `ai-review-gate` (`if: draft == false`) and to `fix_request()` — there is no window in which a person sees the candidate first.

**2. The publisher grants itself the enrollment label.** `docs/policies/github-automation.md:114-115` presents `heleos-delivery` as the control that limits unattended merging: *"Only PRs with `heleos-delivery` are eligible for the merge controller."* `delivery_controller.evaluate()` line 71 enforces it. But line 151 applies `heleos-delivery` **and** `autofix` to every PR this tool opens, so enrollment is not an independent gate — it is a side effect of publishing. Every published task PR is auto-enrolled both for unattended merge into `main` and for provider autofix requests, with no separate human action.

The residual controls are the `automation-hold` label and the bot approval, and per my comment on `delivery_controller.py:58-60` the latter cannot be supplied by the owner. If enrollment is meant to be the owner's opt-in, the publisher should not apply it.

comments.body:
**Correctness: the bounds the policy claims for autofix are not enforced by this config.**

`docs/policies/github-automation.md:64-67` states the contract as: *"An `autofix` label permits at most two deduplicated CodeRabbit requests for separate stacked candidates on ordinary public-repository PRs. Sensitive paths and CodeRabbit-authored fixes do not re-enter that loop."*

Every one of those bounds lives in `delivery_controller.fix_request()` (lines 95-105: `automation-hold`, the `{'autofix','heleos-delivery'}` label pair, the `SENSITIVE`/`SENSITIVE_FILES` exclusion, the two-request cap, the per-head marker). None of them is expressed here. `auto_review.enabled: true` with `base_branches: ['.*']` plus `finishing_touches.autofix.enabled: true` and `fix_ci.enabled: true` configure the provider repository-wide, independent of any label the controller checks and independent of the sensitive-path list.

Failure scenario: a PR that touches `.github/workflows/delivery.yml` or `CLAUDE.md` carries no `autofix` label, so `fix_request()` correctly returns `None` — but the repository-level `finishing_touches` config still applies to that PR, and anyone who can comment on it can invoke the provider directly. The stated "cannot fix sensitive paths" property holds only for requests the controller itself sends.

Also worth noting that `resolve_merge_conflict: false` is set explicitly while `autofix`/`fix_ci` are set to `true`; given that the delivery path is unattended, the conservative default would be the reverse until the pilot in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-automatic-task-delivery.md` Task 3 has actually run.
